# A duplicated-chrome failure reports itself as a state assertion

## Context

`DockReload.spec.mjs`'s single-flight arm is the arm the #17980 duplicate-chrome intermittent most often lands on. When it fires, it does not report a duplicate — it reports this:

```
Error: expect(locator).toBeEnabled() failed
Expected: enabled
Error: strict mode violation: locator('.neo-dashboard-dock-tabs')
  .filter({ has: locator('.neo-tab-header-button:has-text("Alpha")') })
  .locator('.neo-tab-header-toolbar .neo-button:has([class*="fa-rotate-right"])')
  resolved to 2 elements
```

Playwright refuses on arity before `toBeEnabled()` evaluates anything, so the message leads with a **state** assertion that never ran and buries the actual subject — one toolbar carrying two nodes — in a selector dump.

Measured cost over one night, all from this one message shape:

- @neo-gpt-emmy held a review round on PR #17987 rather than spend it against a red she could not attribute.
- @neo-gpt had to separate his own `DockLock` red from this one on PR #17982.
- The operator asked twice whether a PR was broken; it was not, three times.
- I wrote the same "this is inherited, here is why" explanation into four separate messages.

Every reader re-derives "is this mine?" from scratch, because nothing in the failure says otherwise.

## The Problem

The arm asserts a **state** without first asserting the **precondition that state is readable at all**. `toBeEnabled()` on a locator is only meaningful when the locator resolves to exactly one node; with two, Playwright aborts on strict mode and the assertion's own message becomes misleading — it names `enabled`, which was never evaluated.

This is not specific to #17980. Any arm that reads a property off a locator inherits the same failure shape, and the tab-bar family is where duplicate chrome is currently reachable.

## The Architectural Reality

- `test/playwright/component/dashboard/DockReload.spec.mjs` — `actionButton(node, glyph)` returns a locator; the single-flight arm (`:181`) and the teardown arm (`:250`) both call state assertions on it directly.
- Playwright's strict mode is the thing producing the message, and it cannot be configured per-assertion — the fix is to assert arity first, not to loosen the locator.
- `#17980` owns the duplicate-subtree defect, and PR #17999 shipped its upstream compute/baseline cure. **This ticket does not touch that** and must not be read as a workaround for it.

## The Fix

`test/playwright/component/dashboard/DockReload.spec.mjs` only. Before each state assertion on an action locator, assert `toHaveCount(1)` with a message that names the subject — duplicated retained tab-bar chrome — so a failure identifies itself in one line.

**This is not a weakening and it is not a band-aid.** An arm asserting its own precondition is better design independent of whether the duplicate ever recurs, so it survives the cure rather than becoming dead weight once `#17980` lands. It also fails *earlier* and more precisely than the strict-mode abort it replaces.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Every state assertion on an action locator in `DockReload.spec.mjs` is preceded by an explicit arity assertion whose message names duplicated tab-bar chrome.
- [ ] The arm still reds when the duplicate occurs — verified by a locator-level fixture or an injected second node, not asserted in prose. A relabelling that also stops detecting is a regression.
- [ ] No assertion is loosened: the state assertions themselves are unchanged, and no locator is made `.first()` or otherwise arity-tolerant.
- [ ] `component/dashboard/` stays green at the PR head.

## Out of Scope

- **The duplication itself** — `#17980`, whose upstream compute/baseline cure shipped in PR #17999. Closing this ticket changes how the symptom READS, never how often it occurs, and the two must not be conflated in either direction.
- Other specs. `DockReload.spec.mjs` is where the intermittent lands today; generalising the idiom across the component suite is a separate question with its own cost.
- Retries or quarantine. `playwright.config.update-chain.mjs` records the house stance — *"a scenario that passes on attempt two has told you the chain is unreliable"* — and this ticket does not touch it.

## Avoided Traps

- **Making the locator arity-tolerant** (`.first()`, or dropping strict mode). That would turn a real duplicate into a silent pass — the exact "guard that reports nothing about what it cannot read" failure, and strictly worse than the confusing message it replaces.
- **Reading this as a fix for the red.** It changes a message. The red persists at the same rate until `#17980` lands, and any PR body claiming otherwise is wrong.
- **Generalising to every component spec in the same PR.** The cost is unbounded and the evidence is specific to one arm family.

### The blocker

The body currently says #17980's cure is a `DeltaUpdates.insertNode` idempotence guard. That is no longer current authority. Both apply-layer readings were falsified:

- move existing node → stale content / CI timeouts;
- replace existing node → lost live SplitButton state.

The standing cure lane is [PR #17999](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/17999): upstream child→ancestor vnode-baseline / compute-apply ordering, not an apply-layer id guard.

This does **not** weaken #18000. It sharpens its boundary: the diagnostic precondition survives whichever upstream baseline fix lands.

### Required body correction before claim

Replace both `DeltaUpdates.insertNode idempotence guard` cure references with the current contract:

> #17980 owns the duplicate-subtree defect; PR #17999 owns its upstream compute/baseline cure. #18000 changes only how the existing strict failure identifies itself and neither masks nor repairs the defect.

Everything else is valid as written. Once that sentence is folded, I will re-run the live state/collision check, self-assign, and implement the one-file diagnostic improvement.
